editorial_tables.py accepts only the complete 128-trial, 640-method-fit, 1920-stage menu report and the configured numerical source. It requires exactly eight economic-dimension work cells, three stages and five methods per stage.

The generator checks all sixteen finite positive complete shared confirmation clocks per cell, reproduces their mean and requires the same full clock population for every method and stage. It prints the observed mean, minimum and maximum without inventing independent method-specific confirmation timings.

The generated table and its receipt bind the complete report SHA256, numerical source, generator SHA256 and table SHA256. The default command checks exact existing bytes; only explicit --write creates the author table before D.

build.py --publication checks publication_ready and invokes the shared-work utility in its default byte-exact check mode before compiling. A failing utility exits nonzero through subprocess.run(check=True) and stops the workflow before publication.

The frozen workflow runs build --publication before the complete scientific audit and final publisher. Sparse publication-input enumeration materializes the helper, build script, author table and receipt from D, and the publication-input gate compares these D-bound Git leaves.

The shared confirmation bundle covers all five methods, all three stages, the reference and the scalar exercise. Charging the complete bundle to one procedure is explicitly a conservative allocation; the table does not report one fifth of this bill as a measured standalone verification job.

checks: editorial_hjb_diagnostics.py reads three fixed-SHA JSON sources and the declared source/evidence identities; it imports no scientific simulator, model, optimizer or random generator. It requires all 64 trials, 256 candidates and 2048 saved checkpoints.

The HJB helper reconstructs residual-only checkpoint and configuration selection, keeps all four configurations including the configuration never selected, and produces all 32 configuration, 8 untouched-audit and 48 trace-probe rows.

Candidate fit seconds remain a component clock, not an entire deployment cost. Successive-iterate value/policy changes and untouched residuals are descriptive; they are not optimal-value errors or global HJB solution certificates. The probe variance concerns the unhalved covariance-Hessian trace, before the generator factor one half.

The complete HJB report has all 64 selected checkpoints at lbfgs_final after adam_1200. Both Gaussian and Rademacher-with-exact-common trace probes retain their 2/8/32 nested prefixes, 64 states and 64 conditional banks.

The HJB helper binds report, protocol and design SHA256, generator SHA256, table SHA256 and diagnostic extrema in a reproducible receipt. Its default command byte-checks existing table and receipt; explicit --write is the only author-generation mode.

The latest editorial_tables.py keeps the full 128 shared confirmation clocks and adds a presentation copy of the immutable menu comparison table. Exactly one nonexistent mean-column description changes to point estimator underlying each interval; exact reverse replacement must reproduce every source character, preserving all numerical cells.

build.py --publication invokes both presentation helpers in default byte-check mode after publication_ready and before any compilation. Both use subprocess.run(check=True), so a mismatch stops compilation and subsequent publication.

The existing D-bound publication-input enumeration and audit include both helpers, build.py, the author tables and their receipts; the publication workflow still builds before the final complete audit and publisher.
